note: Team marks a guide prints two ways, looked up in an outside source. The row with the other value is dropped and the mark says who checked it. 0.99: `redate` is a game the guide prints under a wrong date (the right one found in ESPN's box scores); `drop` is a printed game that is not this mark (the box score has the number on the other side, or the guide marks it as a playoff game); `revalue` is a number another guide and the box score both correct. 0.99.1: `undate` keeps a mark's number and drops the game the guide prints for it (the box score of that night has another number, and the right night is not known). A `marks` row whose value is the printed one records that an outside box score confirms the print where ESPN's page differs. 0.100: points by half, quarter and overtime are checked against ESPN's line scores (tools/check-period-points.mjs). A `redate` row may carry `opp` where the guide names the wrong opponent as well. `add` is a game that beats the printed mark and is not on the guide's page: it is in ESPN's line score and in a second source (the other team's guide, or a game report), both named. The same `add` rule holds for whole-game marks found by tools/sweep-team-marks.mjs (every ESPN box score since 1993-94): only hits the other team's guide prints for the same night are added.
